On the right is the mother's television, labeled Ratio 4:3; the gray picture horizontally fills the width of the television, but there are uncovered white horizontal regions at the top and bottom. Reasoning: Treat all ratios as width:height. My television and this picture have ratio 16:9. Because the picture only fills the width on the mother's television, let the width of the mother's television also be 16. The ratio of the mother's television is 4:3, so when the width is 16, the height is 12. When the picture has the same width 16, its height is 9. The total uncovered height is 12 - 9 = 3, the uncovered area is 16 × 3, and the total area of the mother's television is 16 × 12. The uncovered fraction is (16 × 3)/(16 × 12) = 3/12 = 1/4.
